question: The shipped supervised blind-spot complement is logistic regression over one-hot substitution tokens -- an ADDITIVE model, the weakest member of the supervised family. Its leave-one-STUDY-out blind-spot AUROC (RT 0.8102, IN 0.8923) is therefore a FLOOR, not a ceiling. Does a CONTEXT-aware estimator beat it on the same data, same split, same subset, same bar?

prior_evidence_stated_up_front.detail: constrained pairwise-interaction vs additive on Stanford fold-change: 2 of 24 powered drug-cells CI-positive (8.3%)
prior_evidence_stated_up_front.why_this_run_is_not_a_duplicate: that run scored the CONTINUOUS log10 fold-change on the FULL cohort under plain KFold. This run scores the BLIND-SPOT subset (catalog-negative isolates) as CLASSIFICATION under leave-one-STUDY-out -- the framing the shipped deployability number actually uses. The blind spot is where the catalog is silent, so it is enriched for non-canonical and accessory patterns, which is precisely where interactions could matter and where the earlier run never looked. It also adds a NON-LINEAR learner, not only explicit pairs.
prior_evidence_stated_up_front.expectation: the prior makes a large win UNLIKELY. This bar is written so that a negative is a publishable closure of the question rather than a shrug, and so a small positive cannot be inflated.

design.pi_excluded_and_why: PI's blind spot holds 3 R of 910 -- unscoreable (wiki/hiv_deployability_per_gene_2026-09-30.json)
design.split: GroupKFold by RefID (leave-one-STUDY-out), IDENTICAL to the deployability harness
design.metric: blind-spot AUROC on the catalog-negative subset -- the deployable number, not the overall AUROC
design.fairness: every estimator sees the SAME rows, the SAME folds and the SAME blind-spot mask; only the estimator differs

estimators.linear_floor: LogisticRegression on one-hot substitution tokens (the shipped model)
estimators.pairwise: one-hot + co-occurrence-floored pairwise interactions (reusing hiv_epistasis.build_pairs/augment), same LogisticRegression
estimators.nonlinear: HistGradientBoostingClassifier on the same one-hot -- captures higher-order structure automatically rather than only explicit pairs

anchor.rule: the linear_floor arm must reproduce the measured deployability AUROC per gene within 0.02 (RT 0.8102, IN 0.8923)
anchor.on_miss: REFUSE the whole comparison (exit 3). A context-vs-floor delta measured against a floor that does not reproduce is not a comparison.

verdict_rule.CONTEXT_BEATS_FLOOR: the best context estimator improves blind-spot AUROC by >= +0.02 AND its paired-bootstrap 95% CI lower bound on the delta is > 0, on BOTH genes
verdict_rule.CONTEXT_HELPS_ONE_GENE_ONLY: the above holds on exactly one gene
verdict_rule.LINEAR_FLOOR_IS_THE_CEILING: no context estimator clears +0.02 with a CI-positive delta on either gene
verdict_rule.UNDERPOWERED: a gene's blind spot has fewer than 10 of either class, or no estimator arm completed
verdict_rule.note: the +0.02 threshold is the same tolerance the anchor uses, so a 'win' must exceed the noise band within which the floor itself is considered reproduced. Deltas are reported per gene regardless of verdict.

what_a_negative_would_license: shipping the linear complement as-is, with the floor documented as the measured ceiling for this feature space -- which closes candidate row 5 rather than leaving it open indefinitely. It would NOT license a claim about attention over raw SEQUENCE, which these token features cannot test.
honest_scope: IN-DISTRIBUTION to the Stanford knowledge base; ~96% subtype B.
Leave-one-study-out is the out-of-distribution split, NOT an independent cohort.

The fold labels are right-censored at 100.0 (wiki/hiv_fold_censoring_audit_2026-09-22). The binary label is a threshold at fold >= 3, far below the ceiling, and EVERY estimator sees the identical labels, so censoring cannot favour one arm.
Two genes of ONE virus. A negative here does not generalise to other pathogens.
'Context' here means interactions among substitution tokens. It does NOT test a sequence model over raw residues, which is a different and more expensive question.
